Every port kind in the app, and proof the outline is right on each one

The catalogue Zach asked for: Block's four views, every port-colour family, every edge a port can sit on (including the bottom edge, which only Loop uses), every paint state a port carries, and Branch's and Loop's header/control ports — each shown at a legible zoom in the real running app, with the exact alignment checks that back the screenshot, and resized to extreme sizes to prove the sockets track the port, not the fixture's original dimensions. Loop itself landed on main partway through this review; §3 covers how it was folded in rather than left as a gap. 2026-09-03.

174/174alignment checks pass across every card and resize below
9distinct port-bearing configurations captured live, not mocked
9sizes stress-tested per Block/Branch/Loop, from 140×100 to 1100×190, plus one real drag on the resize handle
3shape types covered — Block, Branch and Loop — sharing one socket contract

1 · What exists, captured live

Block — Port view (the ordinary card)12/12 checks pass

left-edge inputs, right-edge outputs, a mutates argument surfaced as a top-edge effect port, all six port-colour families

Three inputs and three outputs, one of every colour family the app assigns by type — text green, number grey, model blue, latent orange, image purple, any gold. mut is marked mutates, which derives an effect port and moves it to the top edge, sharing the header row rather than taking an input row.

Block — Simple view (chromeless)4/4 checks pass

subtle ports (hidden until canvas-hover), the exact case this bug shipped in

A Simple Block's ports are subtle — invisible until the pointer is over the canvas, so the title stays uncluttered. This is the view whose outline used to skip the socket entirely: selected and hovered here, at the state that used to draw the selection edge straight through the dot. See the bug-fix report for the before/after.

Block — Value view (the pill)4/4 checks pass

rim ports on a capsule body, no header, no rows

A Value Block is a variable, not a call: one rim dot on each side of the pill, no header band and no port rows to lay them into — the smallest port geometry in the app, and a different body shape (Stadium2d, not a rounded rect) for the socket to sit against.

Block — Expanded view (a container)6/6 checks pass

a frame-like Block's own boundary ports, alongside a nested child Block's ports one level in

Expanded is the one view that holds children — the Container block here has its own boundary ports (p, q in, r out) plus a real child Block nested inside it, each with its own independent socket-correct outline.

Block — dense stress case24/24 checks pass

six ports a side, every colour family, to prove the socket holds as row count grows

Twelve ports on one card is well past anything a real board is likely to need — included because a bug that only shows up past N rows is exactly the kind a normal two-port fixture would never catch.

Block — connected + many-to-one2/2 checks pass

a wired port's filled, type-coloured core; a many-to-one producer-count badge

Two source Blocks feed one sink input. A wired port paints a filled core in its own type colour instead of a hollow ring, and two or more producers into the same port add a count badge — both are extra paint on the very same .Port div, so the outline math is identical to an empty port, but it is included so "every possible port" also means every paint state a port can carry.

Block — unconnected, with a default value2/2 checks pass

Port_default — a filled, muted core with no cable and no badge

An input with a default value and no cable paints a filled core too — muted grey rather than the port's type colour, because nothing is actually flowing through it yet — the third and last paint state a Block's own port carries.

Branch — control ports4/4 checks pass

a second shape type's ports, living on a region's band rather than on a Block

Branch is not a Block: it is a frame-like region whose control ports (cond, value) sit on its header band and decide which arm runs. A structurally different shape, with its own getIndicatorPath — proof the fix's reasoning, and the constant it introduced, generalises past the one class it shipped in.

Loop — header ports4/4 checks pass

the `for`/`while` header's iterable inlet and item outlet, the one port ever placed on a shape's BOTTOM edge

Loop landed on main mid-review — this catalogue named it a gap and it stopped being one before merge. iterable lands on the left wall exactly like a Branch control port; item leaves the header's bottom edge, perpendicular, straight down into the body — the one edge no Block port or Branch control ever sits on, and the edge that specifically exercises the outward-probe direction math. Loop's own getIndicatorPath shipped with the identical hand-copied magic radius Block and Branch had, fixed here alongside them rather than merged as a third copy of the same footgun.

2 · Resized to extremes, still socket-correct

The port dot's position is layoutBlock/branchLayout/loopLayout output — a pure function of props.w/props.h — recomputed on every resize, so a resize is the one live edit most likely to desync the outline from the paint again. Every card below is the same Block, Branch or Loop, driven through the real editor.resizeShape API (the same call a dragged handle makes) across a tiny/small/large/very-wide/very-tall/square matrix, plus one genuine mouse drag on the actual bottom-right resize handle — ten intermediate move events, not a single jump. 72/72 checks pass.

tiny140×100px4/4

Small enough to squeeze rows — the sockets stay put, not the row spacing's problem to solve.

small220×160px10/10

Default-ish proportions, well under the fixture's starting 300×240.

large700×560px10/10

Comfortably larger than any real Block is likely to need.

very-wide1000×160px10/10

Width far past height — the aspect ratio that pushed the outward existence probe off the actual rendered canvas before this suite's own zoom-safety cap was added.

very-tall200×780px10/10

Height far past width — the opposite extreme, same result.

square420×420px10/10

1:1, the one aspect ratio nothing above tests on its own.

branch-large900×700px4/4

Branch resized large — reconcileBranchProps spreads the height delta across both open arms rather than just stretching a body, a different code path from Block's resize.

loop-large900×600px4/4

Loop resized large — reconcileLoopProps floors it at 300×180 and otherwise just stretches the body; iterable and item stay exactly where loopLayout puts them.

dragged10/10

Not `resizeShape` called directly — a real mouse press, ten intermediate move events, and a release on the actual bottom-right resize handle, the literal gesture a person makes.

3 · Loop landed mid-review — here's what changed

This report originally said the Loop region didn't exist yet. It does now.

The first pass of this catalogue found no for/while shape in the codebase and said so plainly, pointing at the design-stage loop-region babble (five directions, L1 — "cycle as a cable" — provisionally ahead) rather than fabricating a screenshot of something unbuilt. Between then and merge, src/loop/LoopShapeUtil.tsx landed on main for real. Re-running this suite against the new code found two things: the port geometry itself is correct (all 16 Loop-related checks below pass), and getIndicatorPath shipped with the exact same hand-copied magic radius (9 instead of LOOP_PORT_RADIUS + 3) that Block and Branch had — not yet a live bug there, since Loop's ports are never subtle, but the identical footgun, fixed alongside the other two rather than left to become a fourth copy of it later.

The shipped design also answers the babble's open question directly: Loop does not use a distinct "loop header port" glyph. iterable and item are ordinary .Port dots — same component, same CSS, same connection rules Block and Branch already have — placed on the header via elbowSide: 'left' and elbowSide: 'bottom'. One socket contract, a third shape using it.

4 · How "verified" is measured

Every card's badge is read from npm run test:port-alignment's own results file — the same run that captured the screenshots, not a second pass. Two independent claims per port: the computed indicator centre lands within 1px of the live .Port dot's getBoundingClientRect centre (measured through the app's real getShapePageTransform + editor.pageToScreen, never a screenshot diff), and the live selection-overlay canvas actually has ink at a point sitting on the socket's own outer edge — the one place a skipped port (the bug this suite guards) paints nothing at all. See the original bug-fix report for the full method and the regression proof.
